card.name: Itik-Itik
card.profile: Itik-itik is a mimetic Philippine folk dance based on the movements of the itik (duck), originating in Cantilan, Surigao del Sur and documented by National Artist Francisca Reyes-Aquino. Folklore traces it to a dancer named Kanang who, performing the Sibay at a baptism, improvised short choppy steps imitating ducks splashing water; spectators imitated her and it spread. Derived from the Sibay bird dance; performed to rondalla music, men in barong tagalog, women in baro’t saya.
card.insight: A 2019 movement analysis found Itik-itik engages shoulders, hips, knees and deltoids with precise heel-toe patterns — "technique is subtle, not absent." (Asian Journal of Interdisciplinary Research)

observation.setting: Indoor stage performance with a large Philippine flag backdrop and an audience seated in the foreground
observation.formation_and_space: Starting in a line, moving into pairs, columns, and circular formations across the stage
observation.posture: Upright torso, slightly bent knees with soft weight changes
observation.footwork: Rhythmic stepping side-to-side, toe taps, and small weight shifts on the beat
observation.arms_and_hands: Arms held at waist or shoulder height with fluttering wrist and hand movements, occasional clapping
observation.hips_and_torso: Subtle hip sways and upper body tilts corresponding to arm gestures
observation.partnering: Dancing in pairs holding hands or linking arms at various moments
observation.levels_jumps_turns: Low to medium level, graceful turns and pivots without high jumps
observation.costume_and_props: Matching yellow and black plaid dresses with short puffed sleeves and yellow hair ribbons, bare feet
observation.cannot_infer: Exact foot placement and fast weight transfers are partially obscured by the long dresses and camera distance.

signature_moments.what: Pairs of dancers hold hands and circle each other while making fluid arm gestures
Dancers link inside hands and pivot in place with lively foot taps
